exampleAnswers.title: Finding the Limit of a Vector Function

question.text: Calculate $\displaystyle \lim_{t \to 2}\mathbf f(t),$ if $\mathbf f(t) = \left \langle e^{t-2}, \, \sqrt{6-t}, \, \dfrac{3}{t+2} \right \rangle.$
question.explanation:
First, recall that \[ \lim_{t \to 2}\mathbf f(t) = \left \langle \lim_{t \to 2} e^{t-2}, \, \lim_{t \to 2} \sqrt{6-t}, \, \lim_{t \to 2} \dfrac{3}{t+2} \right\rangle. \]

Now, we find the limits one by one.

  • For the first component, we have \begin{align*} \lim_{t \to 2} e^{t-2} & = e^{2-2} \\[3pt] &= e^0 \\[3pt] &= 1. \end{align*}

  • For the second component, we have \begin{align*} \lim_{t \to 2} \sqrt{6-t} & = \sqrt{6-2} \\[3pt] & = \sqrt{4} \\[3pt] & = 2 . \end{align*}

  • For the third component, we have \begin{align*} \lim_{t \to 2} \dfrac{3}{t+2} &= \dfrac{3}{2+2} \\[5pt] & = \dfrac{3}{4}. \end{align*}

Hence, $\lim\limits_{t \to 2}\mathbf f(t) = \left \langle 1, 2 , \dfrac{3}{4} \right \rangle.$

example.title: Finding the Limit of a Vector Function

question.text: Calculate $\displaystyle \lim_{s\to 1} \mathbf f(s),$ if $\mathbf f(s) = \begin{bmatrix}\sqrt{5-s} \\ \dfrac{e^{1-s}}{s} \\ (1+5s)^{1-s} \end{bmatrix}.$
question.explanation:
First, recall that \[ \lim_{s \to 1}\mathbf f(s) = \begin{bmatrix} \displaystyle\lim_{s \to 1} \sqrt{5-s} \\ \displaystyle \lim_{s \to 1} \dfrac{e^{1-s}}{s} \\ \displaystyle \lim_{s \to 1} \, (1+5s)^{1/(2s)}. \end{bmatrix} \]

Now, we find the limits one by one.

  • For the first component, we have \begin{align*} \lim_{s \to 1} \sqrt{5-s} &= \sqrt{5-1} \\[5pt] &= \sqrt{4} \\[5pt] &= 2. \end{align*}

  • For the second component, we have \begin{align*} \lim_{s \to 1} \dfrac{e^{1-s}}{s} = \dfrac{e^{1-1}}{1} = 1. \end{align*}

  • For the third component, we have \begin{align*} \lim_{s \to 1} \, (1+5s)^{1-s} & = (1 + 5 \cdot 1)^{1-1}\\[5pt] & = 6^0\\[5pt] & = 1. \end{align*}

Hence, $\lim\limits_{s \to 1}\mathbf f(s) = \begin{bmatrix} 2 \\ 1 \\ 1 \end{bmatrix}.$

example.title: Finding the Limit of a Vector Function

question.text: Calculate $\displaystyle \lim_{s \to 2}\mathbf f(s)$, if $\mathbf f(s) = \left \langle \dfrac 5 {e^{s-2}}, \, 3\cos(4-2s), \, s^3-5 \right \rangle.$
question.explanation:
First, recall that \[ \lim_{s \to 2}\mathbf f(s) = \left \langle \lim_{s \to 2} \dfrac 5 {e^{s-2}}, \, \lim_{s \to 2} 3\cos(4-2s), \, \lim_{s \to 2} \, (s^3 - 5) \right\rangle. \]

Now, we find the limits one by one.

  • For the first component, we have \begin{align*} \lim_{s \to 2} \dfrac 5 {e^{s-2}} &= \dfrac{5}{e^{2-2}} = 5. \end{align*}

  • For the first component, we have \begin{align*} \lim_{s \to 2} 3 \cos(4-2s) &= 3 \displaystyle \lim_{s \to 2} \cos(4-2s) \\[5pt] & = 3 \cdot \cos(4 - 2 \cdot 2) \\[5pt] & = 3 \cdot \cos{0} \\[5pt] & = 3 . \end{align*}

  • For the third component, we have \begin{align*} \lim_{s \to 2} \, (s^3 - 5) &= 2^3 - 5 = 3. \end{align*}

Hence, $\lim\limits_{s \to 2}\mathbf f(s) = \left \langle 5, 3, 3 \right \rangle.$

example.title: Finding the Limit of a Vector Function

question.text: Find the limit $\displaystyle \lim_{t \to 0}\mathbf f(t),$ if $\mathbf f(t) = \sin{t} \,\mathbf i + \cos{t}\, \mathbf j + (t+2)^2\, \mathbf k.$
question.explanation:
First, recall that \[ \lim_{t \to 0}\mathbf f(t) = \left(\lim_{t \to 0} \sin{t}\right) \mathbf i + \left(\lim_{t \to 0} \cos{t}\right) \mathbf j + \left(\lim_{t \to 0} (t+2)^2 \right) \mathbf k . \]

Now, we find the limits one-by-one.

  • For the first component, we have \begin{align*} \lim\limits_{t \to 0} \sin{t} &= \sin{0} = 0. \end{align*}

  • For the second component, we have \begin{align*} \lim_{t \to 0} \cos{0} = 1. \end{align*}

  • For the third component, we have \begin{align*} \lim_{t \to 0} \, (t+2)^2 &= (0+2)^2=4. \end{align*}

Hence, $\lim\limits_{t \to 0}\mathbf f(t) = \mathbf j + 4\,\mathbf k.$

example.title: Finding the Limit of a Vector Function

question.text: Calculate $\displaystyle \lim_{s\to 0} \mathbf f(s)$, if $\mathbf f(s) = \begin{bmatrix}\sqrt{s+8} \\ \dfrac{\arcsin s}{s} \\ (1+2s)^{1/(2s)} \end{bmatrix}.$
question.explanation:
First, recall that: \[ \lim_{s \to 0}\mathbf f(s) = \begin{bmatrix} \displaystyle\lim_{s \to 0} \sqrt{s+8} \\ \displaystyle \lim_{s \to 0} \dfrac{\arcsin s}{s} \\ \displaystyle \lim_{s \to 0} (1+2s)^{1/(2s)} \end{bmatrix} \]

Now, we find the limits one-by-one.

  • For the first component, we have: \begin{align*} \lim_{s \to 0} \sqrt{s+8} &= \sqrt{0+8} \\[3pt] &= \sqrt{8} \\[3pt] &= \sqrt{2^3} \\[3pt] &= 2\sqrt{2} \end{align*}

  • The second component can be found using L'Hopital's Rule: \begin{align*} \lim_{s \to 0} \dfrac{\arcsin s}{s} & = \displaystyle \lim_{s \to 0} \dfrac{\left(\arcsin s\right)'}{s'} \\[3pt] & = \displaystyle \lim_{s \to 0} \dfrac{\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{1-s^2}}}{1}\\[3pt] & = \displaystyle \lim_{s \to 0} \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{1-s^2}}\\[3pt] &= \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{1-0^2}} \\[3pt] &= 1 \end{align*}

  • The third component can be found using a special limit: \begin{align*} \lim_{s \to 0} (1+2s)^{1/(2s)} &= \displaystyle{\lim_{u \to 0} (1+u)^{1/u}} = e \end{align*}

Hence, $\lim\limits_{s \to 0}\mathbf f(s) = \begin{bmatrix} 2\sqrt{2} \\ 1 \\ e \end{bmatrix}.$

exampleAnswers.title: Finding the Limit of the Magnitude of a Vector Function

question.text: Calculate $\displaystyle \lim_{s \to 1}\mathbf \| \mathbf f(s) \|,$ if $\mathbf f(s) = \begin{bmatrix}\sqrt{5-s} \\ \dfrac{e^{1-s}}{s} \\ (1+5s)^{1-s} \end{bmatrix}.$
question.explanation:
First, recall that \[ \lim_{s \to 1}\mathbf f(s) = \begin{bmatrix} \displaystyle\lim_{s \to 1} \sqrt{5-s} \\ \displaystyle \lim_{s \to 1} \dfrac{e^{1-s}}{1-s} \\ \displaystyle \lim_{s \to 1} \, (1+5s)^{1/(2s)} \end{bmatrix}. \]

Now, we find the limits one by one.

  • For the first component, we have \begin{align*} \lim_{s \to 1} \sqrt{5-s} &= \sqrt{5-1} \\[5pt] &= \sqrt{4} \\[5pt] &= 2. \end{align*}

  • For the second component, we have \begin{align*} \lim_{s \to 1} \dfrac{e^{1-s}}{s} = \dfrac{1}{1} = 1. \end{align*}

  • For the third component, we have \begin{align*} \lim_{s \to 1} \, (1+5s)^{1-s} &= (1+5 \cdot 1)^{1-1} = 1. \end{align*}

Hence, $\lim\limits_{s \to 1}\mathbf f(s) = \begin{bmatrix} 2 \\ 1 \\ 1 \end{bmatrix}.$

Finally, the limit of $\left\| \mathbf f(s) \right\|$ as $s$ approaches $1$ is \begin{align*} \lim_{s \to 1} \left\|\mathbf f(s) \right\| & = \left\| \displaystyle \lim_{s \to 1}\mathbf f(s) \right\| \\[5pt] & = \left\| \begin{bmatrix} 2 \\ 1 \\ 1 \end{bmatrix} \right\| \\[5pt] & = \sqrt{2^2+1^2+1^2} \\[5pt] & = \sqrt{6}. \end{align*}

example.title: Finding the Limit of the Magnitude of a Vector Function

question.text: Calculate $\displaystyle \lim_{s \to 0}\mathbf \| \mathbf f(s) \|$, if $\mathbf f(s) = \begin{bmatrix}\dfrac {s}{(s+1)^2} \\ \dfrac{\sin^2 s}{s^2} \\ \dfrac {1-\cos s}{2s^2} \end{bmatrix}\!.$
question.explanation:
First, recall that:

\begin{align*} \lim_{s \to 0}\mathbf f(s) & = \begin{bmatrix} \displaystyle \lim_{s \to 0} \dfrac{s}{(s+1)^2} \\ \displaystyle \lim_{s \to 0} \dfrac{\sin^2 s}{s^2} \\ \displaystyle \lim_{s \to 0} \dfrac{1-\cos s}{2s^2} \end{bmatrix} \end{align*}

Now, we find the limits one-by-one.

  • For the first component, we have: \begin{align*} \lim_{s \to 0} \dfrac{s}{(s+1)^2} &= \dfrac{0}{(0+1)^2} = 0 \\[5pt] \end{align*}

  • The second component can be found using a special limit: \begin{align*} \lim_{s \to 0} \dfrac{\sin^2 s}{s^2} &= \lim_{s \to 0} \left(\dfrac{\sin s}{s}\right)^2 \\[3pt] &= \left(\lim_{s \to 0} \dfrac{\sin s}{s}\right)^2 \\[3pt] &= 1^2 \\[3pt] &= 1 \\[5pt] \end{align*}

  • The third component can be found using L'Hopital's Rule twice: \begin{align*} \lim_{s \to 0} \dfrac{1-\cos s}{2s^2} &= \displaystyle \lim_{s \to 0} \dfrac{\left(1-\cos s\right)''}{\left(2s^2\right)''} \\[3pt] &= \displaystyle \lim_{s \to 0} \dfrac{\cos s}{4} \\[3pt] &= \dfrac{\cos 0}{4} \\[3pt] &= \dfrac{1}{4}\\[5pt] \end{align*}

Hence, $ \lim\limits_{s \to 0}\mathbf f(s) = \begin{bmatrix} 0 \\ 1 \\ {1}/{4} \end{bmatrix}\!.$

Finally, the limit of $\left\| \mathbf f(s) \right\|$ as $s$ approaches $0$ is: \begin{align*} \lim_{s \to 0} \left\|\mathbf f(s) \right\| & = \left\| \displaystyle \lim_{s \to 0}\mathbf f(s) \right\| \\[3pt] & = \left\| \begin{bmatrix} 0 \\ 1 \\ {1}/{4} \end{bmatrix} \right\| \\[3pt] & = \sqrt{0^2+1^2+\left(\dfrac{1}{4}\right)^2} \\[3pt] % & = \sqrt {1+\dfrac{1}{16}} \\[3pt] &= \sqrt{\dfrac{17}{16}} \\[3pt] &= \dfrac{\sqrt{17}}{4} \end{align*}

example.title: Finding the Limit of the Magnitude of a Vector Function

question.text: Find the limit $\displaystyle \lim_{t \to 1} \| \mathbf f(t) \|$, if $\mathbf f(t) = \dfrac {4+t}5 \,\mathbf i + \dfrac{\sin(t-1)}{t^2 - 1}\, \mathbf j + \sqrt {9t}\, \mathbf k.$
question.explanation:
First, recall that:

\begin{align*} \lim_{t \to 1}\mathbf f(t) & = \left( \lim_{t \to 1} \dfrac{4+t}{5}\right) \,\mathbf i + \left( \lim_{t \to 1} \dfrac{\sin(t-1)}{t^2-1}\right) \, \mathbf j + \left( \lim_{t \to 1} \sqrt{9t} \right) \, \mathbf k \end{align*}

Now, we find the limits one-by-one.

  • For the first component, we have: \begin{align*} \lim_{t \to 1} \dfrac{4+t}{5} &= \dfrac{4+1}{5} = 1 \\[5pt] \end{align*}

  • The second component can be found using a special limit: \begin{align*} \lim_{t \to 1} \dfrac{\sin(t-1)}{t^2-1} &= \lim_{t \to 1} \dfrac{\sin(t-1)}{(t-1)(t+1)} \\[3pt] &= \left(\displaystyle \lim_{t \to 1} \dfrac{1}{t+1}\right) \cdot \left(\displaystyle \lim_{t \to 1} \dfrac{\sin(t-1)}{t-1}\right) \\[3pt] &= \left(\dfrac{1}{1+1}\right) \cdot 1 \\[3pt] &= \dfrac{1}{2} \\[5pt] \end{align*}

  • For the third component, we have: \begin{align*} \lim_{t \to 1} \sqrt{9t} &= \sqrt{9(1)} = 3 \end{align*}

Hence, $ \lim\limits_{t \to 1}\mathbf f(t) = \mathbf i + \dfrac{1}{2}\,\mathbf j + 3\,\mathbf k.$

Finally, the limit of $\left\| \mathbf f(t) \right\|$ as $t$ approaches $1$ is: \begin{align*} \lim_{t \to 1} \left\|\mathbf f(t) \right\| & = \left\| \displaystyle \lim_{t \to 1}\mathbf f(t) \right\| \\[3pt] & = \left\| \mathbf i + \dfrac{1}{2}\,\mathbf j + 3\,\mathbf k \right\| \\[3pt] & = \sqrt{1^2+\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)^2+3^2} \\[3pt] & = \sqrt{1+\dfrac{1}{4}+9} \\[3pt] & = \sqrt{\dfrac{41}{4}} \\[3pt] & = \dfrac{\sqrt{41}}{2} \end{align*}

example.title: Finding the Limit of the Magnitude of a Vector Function

question.text: Calculate $\displaystyle \lim_{t \to 3}\mathbf \| \mathbf f(t) \|$, if $\mathbf f(t) =\begin{bmatrix} t^2 - 3t \\ \dfrac{1}{t^2-8} \\ 5-2t \end{bmatrix}.$
question.explanation:
First, recall that: \[ \lim_{t \to 3}\mathbf f(t) = \begin{bmatrix} \displaystyle{\lim_{t \to 3} \left(t^2-3t\right)} \\ \displaystyle{\lim_{t \to 3} \dfrac{1}{t^2-8}} \\ \displaystyle{\lim_{t \to 3} (5-2t)} \end{bmatrix} \]

Now, we find the limits one-by-one.

  • For the first component, we have: \begin{align*} \lim_{t \to 3} \left(t^2-3t\right) &= 3^2-3(3) = 0 \end{align*}

  • For the second component, we have: \begin{align*} \lim_{t \to 3} \dfrac{1}{t^2-8} & = \dfrac 1 {3^2-8} = 1 \end{align*}

  • For the third component, we have: \begin{align*} \lim_{t \to 3} (5 - 2t) &= 5 - 2(3) = -1 \end{align*}

Hence, $\lim\limits_{t \to 3}\mathbf f(t) = \begin{bmatrix} 0 \\ 1 \\ -1 \end{bmatrix}.$

Finally, the limit of $\left\| \mathbf f(t) \right\|$ as $t$ approaches $3$ is \begin{align*} \lim_{t \to 3} \left\|\mathbf f(t) \right\| & = \left\| \displaystyle \lim_{t \to 3}\mathbf f(t) \right\| \\[3pt] & = \left\| \begin{bmatrix} 0 \\ 1 \\ -1 \end{bmatrix} \right\| \\[3pt] & = \sqrt{0^2+1^2+(-1)^2} \\[3pt] & = \sqrt{2} \,. \end{align*}

example.title: Finding the Limit of the Magnitude of a Vector Function

question.text: Find the limit $\,\displaystyle \lim_{t \to 0} \left\| \mathbf f(t) \right\|,$ if $\mathbf f(t) = \sin{t} \,\mathbf i + \cos{t}\, \mathbf j + (t+2)^2\, \mathbf k.$
question.explanation:
First, recall that \[ \lim_{t \to 0}\mathbf f(t) = \left(\lim_{t \to 0} \sin{t}\right) \mathbf i + \left(\lim_{t \to 0} \cos{t}\right) \mathbf j + \left(\lim_{t \to 0} (t+2)^2 \right) \mathbf k . \]

Now, we find the limits one by one.

  • For the first component, we have \begin{align*} \lim_{t \to 0} \sin{t} &= \sin{0} = 0. \end{align*}

  • For the second component, we have \begin{align*} \lim_{t \to 0} \cos{0} = 1. \end{align*}

  • For the third component, we have \begin{align*} \lim_{t \to 0}\, (t+2)^2 &= (0+2)^2=4. \end{align*}

Hence, $\lim\limits_{t \to 0}\mathbf f(t) = \mathbf j + 4\,\mathbf k.$

Finally, the limit of $\left\| \mathbf f(t) \right\|$ as $t$ approaches $0$ is \begin{align*} \lim_{t \to 0} \left\|\mathbf f(t) \right\| & = \left\| \displaystyle \lim_{t \to 0}\mathbf f(t) \right\| \\[5pt] & = \left\| \mathbf j + 4\,\mathbf k \right\| \\[5pt] & = \sqrt{1^2+4^2} \\[5pt] & = \sqrt{17}. \end{align*}

exampleAnswers.title: Finding the Limit of a Sum of Vector Functions

question.text:
Find $\displaystyle \lim_{t \to \infty} \left[\mathbf g(t) + 2\mathbf f(t) \right]$ given that $\mathbf f(t)$ and $\mathbf g(t)$ are defined as follows:

\begin{align*} \mathbf f(t) & = \dfrac{t^2}{1-t^2}\,\mathbf i + \left(1+\dfrac{1}{t}\right) \, \mathbf j + t^{-2}\, \mathbf k \\[3pt] \mathbf g(t) & = 2\,\mathbf i + e^{-t}\, \mathbf j + \left(1+\dfrac{1}{t}\right)^t\, \mathbf k \end{align*}
question.explanation:
First, we find the limit of each function: \begin{align} \lim_{t \to \infty} \mathbf f(t) & = \left( \lim_{t \to \infty} \dfrac{t^2}{1-t^2} \right) \,\mathbf i + \left( \lim_{t \to \infty} \left(1+\dfrac{1}{t}\right) \right)\, \mathbf j - \left( \lim_{t \to \infty} t^{-2} \right)\, \mathbf k ,\\[5pt] \lim_{t \to \infty} \mathbf g(t) & = \left( \lim_{t \to \infty} 2 \right) \,\mathbf i - \left( \lim_{t \to \infty} e^{-t} \right)\,\mathbf j + \left( \lim_{t \to \infty} \left(1+\dfrac{1}{t}\right)^t \right)\, \mathbf k. \end{align}

Let's find the limits one-by-one.

\begin{align*} &\lim_{t \to \infty} \dfrac{t^2}{1-t^2} = \lim_{t \to \infty} \dfrac{1}{\dfrac{1}{t^2}-1} = -1\\[5pt] &\lim_{t \to \infty} \left(1+\dfrac{1}{t}\right) = 1+ \lim_{t \to \infty} \dfrac{1}{t} = 1\\[5pt] &\lim_{t \to \infty} t^{-2} = \lim_{t \to \infty} \dfrac{1}{t^2} = 0\\[5pt] &\lim_{t \to \infty} 2 = 2\\[5pt] &\lim_{t \to \infty} e^{-t} = 0\\[5pt] &\lim_{t \to \infty} \left(1+\dfrac{1}{t}\right)^t = e \end{align*}

So, we get:

\begin{align} \lim_{t \to \infty} \mathbf f(t) & = -1 \,\mathbf i + 1\, \mathbf j + 0\, \mathbf k \\[3pt] & = - \mathbf i + \mathbf j ,\\[5pt] \lim_{t \to \infty} \mathbf g(t) & = 2 \,\mathbf i + 0\, \mathbf j + e\, \mathbf k \\[3pt] & = 2\, \mathbf i + e\, \mathbf k. \end{align}

Now, we use properties of limits to calculate the final result:

\begin{align} \lim_{t \to \infty} \left[ \mathbf g(t) + 2\mathbf f(t) \right] & = \lim_{t \to \infty}\mathbf g(t) + 2\lim_{t \to \infty}\mathbf f(t) \\[3pt] & = \big( 2\, \mathbf i + e\, \mathbf k \big) + 2\big( - \mathbf i + \mathbf j \big) \\[3pt] & = 2\mathbf j + e\, \mathbf k \end{align}

example.title: Finding the Limit of a Sum of Vector Functions

question.text:
Find $\displaystyle \lim_{t \to 0} \big[ \mathbf f(t) + 4\mathbf g(t) \big]$ given that $\mathbf f(t)$ and $\mathbf g(t)$ are defined as

\begin{align*} \mathbf f(t) = \begin{bmatrix} 3e^t \\ \tan{t} \\ \dfrac{t^2+9}{t+3} \end{bmatrix}, \qquad \mathbf g(t) = \begin{bmatrix} t-2 \\ \dfrac{3t-2}{t^2-1} \\ 2^t \end{bmatrix}. \end{align*}
question.explanation:
First, we find the limit of each function: \begin{align*} \lim_{t \to 0} \mathbf f(t) & = \begin{bmatrix} \displaystyle \lim_{t \to 0} 3e^t \\ \displaystyle \lim_{t \to 0} \tan{t} \\ \displaystyle \lim_{t \to 0} \dfrac{t^2+9}{t+3} \end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix} 3e^0 \\ \tan{0} \\ \dfrac{0^2+9}{0+3} \end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix} 3 \\ 0 \\ 3 \end{bmatrix}\\[10pt] \lim_{t \to 0} \mathbf g(t) & = \begin{bmatrix} \displaystyle \lim_{t \to 0} \, (t - 2) \\ \displaystyle \lim_{t \to 0} \dfrac{3t-2}{t^2-1} \\ \displaystyle \lim_{t \to 0} 2^t \end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix} 0-2 \\ \dfrac{3(0)-2}{0^2-1} \\ 2^0 \end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix} -2 \\ 2 \\ 1 \end{bmatrix} \end{align*}

Now, we use properties of limits to calculate the final result:

\begin{align*} \lim_{t \to 0} \big[ \mathbf f(t) + 4\mathbf g(t) \big] & = \lim_{t \to 0} \mathbf f(t) + 4 \lim_{t \to 0} \mathbf g(t) \\[5pt] & = \begin{bmatrix} 3 \\ 0 \\ 3 \end{bmatrix} + 4 \begin{bmatrix} -2 \\ 2 \\ 1 \end{bmatrix} \\[5pt] & = \begin{bmatrix} 3 \\ 0 \\ 3 \end{bmatrix} + \begin{bmatrix} -8 \\ 8 \\ 4 \end{bmatrix} \\[5pt] & = \begin{bmatrix} -5 \\ 8 \\ 7 \end{bmatrix} \end{align*}

example.title: Finding the Limit of a Sum of Vector Functions

question.text:
Find $\displaystyle \lim_{t \to 0} [3\mathbf f(t) - \mathbf g(t)]$ given that $\mathbf f(t)$ and $\mathbf g(t)$ are defined as:

\begin{align*} \mathbf f(t) & = \left\langle \cos t, t^2-2 , \dfrac {t-3} {t^2+1} \right\rangle \\[3pt] \mathbf g(t) & = \left\langle \sin t, \sqrt t + \sqrt 2, 2 \right\rangle \end{align*}
question.explanation:
First, we find the limit of each function: \begin{align} \lim_{t \to 0} \mathbf f(t) & = \left\langle \lim_{t \to 0} (\cos t), \: \lim_{t \to 0}(t^2-2) , \: \lim_{t \to 0}\left(\dfrac {t-3} {t^2+1}\right) \right\rangle\\[3pt] & = \left\langle \cos 0, 0^2-2 , \dfrac {0-3} {0^2+1} \right\rangle\\[3pt] & = \left\langle 1, -2 , -3 \right\rangle\\[5pt] \lim_{t \to 0} \mathbf g(t) & = \left\langle \lim_{t \to 0}(\sin t), \: \lim_{t \to 0}(\sqrt t + \sqrt 2), \: \lim_{t \to 0}(2) \right\rangle \\[3pt] & = \left\langle \sin 0, \sqrt 0 + \sqrt 2, 2 \right\rangle \\[3pt] & = \left\langle 0, \sqrt 2, 2 \right\rangle \\ \end{align}

Now, we use properties of limits to calculate the final result:

\begin{align} \lim_{t \to 0} [3\mathbf f(t) - \mathbf g(t)]& = \lim_{t \to 0} 3\mathbf f(t) - \lim_{t \to 0} \mathbf g(t) \\[3pt] & = 3\lim_{t \to 0} \mathbf f(t) - \lim_{t \to 0} \mathbf g(t) \\[3pt] & = 3 \left\langle 1, -2 , -3 \right\rangle - \left\langle 0, \sqrt 2, 2 \right\rangle\\[3pt] & = \left\langle 3, -6 , -9 \right\rangle - \left\langle 0, \sqrt 2, 2 \right\rangle\\[3pt] & = \left\langle 3-0, -6-\sqrt 2 , -9-2 \right\rangle \\[3pt] & = \left\langle 3, -6-\sqrt 2 , -11 \right\rangle \end{align}

example.title: Finding the Limit of a Sum of Vector Functions

question.text:
Find $\displaystyle \lim_{t \to 1} \big[ 5\mathbf f(t) +2 \mathbf g(t) \big]$ given that $\mathbf f(t)$ and $\mathbf g(t)$ are defined as:

\begin{align*} \mathbf f(t) &= \left\langle t^2, t^3 , \dfrac 1 {t^2} \right\rangle \\[3pt] \mathbf g(t) &= \left\langle 5-t^3, t^2-t +2, 4 \right\rangle \end{align*}
question.explanation:
First, we find the limit of each function:

\begin{align*} \lim_{t \to 1} \mathbf f(t) & = \left\langle \lim_{t \to 1} (t^2), \: \lim_{t \to 1}(t^3) ,\: \lim_{t \to 1}\left(\dfrac 1 {t^2}\right) \right\rangle \\[3pt] & = \left\langle 1^2, 1^3 , \dfrac 1 {1^2}\right\rangle \\[3pt] & = \left\langle 1, 1 , 1 \right\rangle \\[5pt] \lim_{t \to 1} \mathbf g(t) & = \left\langle \lim_{t \to 1}(5-t^3),\: \lim_{t \to 1}(t^2-t +2), \: \lim_{t \to 1}(4) \right\rangle \\[3pt] & = \left\langle 5-1^3, 1^2-1 + 2, 4 \right\rangle \\[3pt] & = \left\langle 4, 2, 4 \right\rangle \end{align*}

Now, we use properties of limits to calculate the final result:

\begin{align*} \lim_{t \to 1} \big[ 5\mathbf f(t) +2 \mathbf g(t) \big] & = \lim_{t \to 1} 5\mathbf f(t) + \lim_{t \to 1}2 \mathbf g(t) \\[3pt] & = 5\lim_{t \to 1} \mathbf f(t) + 2\lim_{t \to 1} \mathbf g(t) \\[3pt] & = 5 \left\langle 1, 1 , 1 \right\rangle + 2 \left\langle 4, 2, 4 \right\rangle\\[3pt] & = \left\langle 5, 5 , 5 \right\rangle + \left\langle 8, 4, 8 \right\rangle\\[3pt] & = \left\langle 13, 9 , 13 \right\rangle \end{align*}

example.title: Finding the Limit of a Sum of Vector Functions

question.text:
Find $\displaystyle \lim_{t \to 0} \big[ \mathbf f(t) + \mathbf g(t) \big]$ given that $\mathbf f(t)$ and $\mathbf g(t)$ are defined as:

\begin{align*} \mathbf f(t) = \begin{bmatrix} t^2 \\ e^t \\ \dfrac{\sin{t}}{t} \end{bmatrix}, \qquad \mathbf g(t) = \begin{bmatrix} \cos t \\ 1 \\ \dfrac{2t-1}{t^2+1} \end{bmatrix} \end{align*}
question.explanation:
First, we find the limit of each function:

\begin{align*} \lim_{t \to 0} \mathbf f(t) = \begin{bmatrix} \displaystyle \lim_{t \to 0} t^2 \\ \displaystyle \lim_{t \to 0} e^t \\ \displaystyle \lim_{t \to 0} \dfrac{\sin{t}}{t} \end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix} 0^2 \\ e^0 \\ 1 \end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix} 0 \\ 1 \\ 1 \end{bmatrix}\\[7pt] \end{align*}

Note that the third component is a special limit.

\begin{align*} \lim_{t \to 0} \mathbf g(t) = \begin{bmatrix} \displaystyle \lim_{t \to 0} \cos t \\ \displaystyle \lim_{t \to 0} 1 \\ \displaystyle \lim_{t \to 0} \dfrac{2t-1}{t^2+1} \end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix} \cos 0 \\ 1 \\ \dfrac{2(0)-1}{0^2+1}) \end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix} 1 \\ 1 \\ -1 \end{bmatrix} \end{align*}

Now, we use properties of limits to calculate the final result:

\begin{align*} \lim_{t \to 0} \big[ \mathbf f(t) + \mathbf g(t) \big] & = \lim_{t \to 0} \mathbf f(t) + \lim_{t \to 0} \mathbf g(t) \\[3pt] & = \begin{bmatrix} 0 \\ 1 \\ 1 \end{bmatrix} + \begin{bmatrix} 1 \\ 1 \\ -1\end{bmatrix} \\[3pt] & = \begin{bmatrix} 1 \\ 2 \\ 0 \end{bmatrix} \end{align*}

question.text: Find $\displaystyle \lim_{t \to 2} \big[ \mathbf f(t) \times \mathbf g(t) \big]$ given that $\mathbf f(t)$ and $\mathbf g(t)$ are defined as \begin{align*} \mathbf f(t) &= \left\langle 6-t^3, \, t^2-6 , \, \dfrac{16} {t^3} \right\rangle ,\\[5pt] \mathbf g(t) &= \left\langle 5-\ln(3-t), \, \sqrt{6-t}, \, 2t \right\rangle. \end{align*}
question.explanation:
First, we find the limit of each function:

\begin{align*} \lim_{t \to 2} \mathbf f(t) & = \left\langle \lim_{t \to 2} \, (6-t^3), \, \lim_{t \to 2} \, (t^2-6) ,\, \lim_{t \to 2} \dfrac{16}{t^3} \right\rangle \\[5pt] & = \left\langle 6 - 2^3, 2^2 - 6 , \dfrac{16}{2^3}\right\rangle \\[5pt] & = \left\langle -2, -2 , 2 \right\rangle \\[10pt] \lim_{t \to 2} \mathbf g(t) & = \left\langle \lim_{t \to 2} \, (5-\ln(3-t)),\, \lim_{t \to 2} \, \sqrt{6-t}, \, \lim_{t \to 2} \, 2t \right\rangle \\[5pt] & = \left\langle 5-\ln(3-2), \sqrt{6-2}, 2(2) \right\rangle \\[5pt] & = \left\langle 5, 2, 4 \right\rangle \end{align*}

Now, we use properties of limits to calculate the final result:

\begin{align*} \lim_{t \to 2} \big[ \mathbf f(t) \times \mathbf g(t) \big] & = \lim_{t \to 2} \mathbf f(t) \times \lim_{t \to 2} \mathbf g(t) \\[5pt] & = \left\langle -2, -2 , 2 \right\rangle \times \left\langle 5,2,4 \right\rangle \\[5pt] &= \left| \begin{array}{ccc} \mathbf{i} & \mathbf{j} & \mathbf{k} \\ -2 & -2 & 2 \\ 5 & 2 & 4 \end{array} \right| \\[5pt] &= \left| \begin{array}{cc} -2 & 2 \\ 2 & 4 \end{array} \right| \mathbf{i} - \left| \begin{array}{cc} -2 & 2 \\ 5 & 4 \end{array} \right| \mathbf{j} + \left| \begin{array}{cc} -2 & -2 \\ 5 & 2 \end{array} \right| \mathbf{k} \\[5pt] & = ((-2) \cdot 4 - 2 \cdot 2) \, \mathbf{i} - ((-2) \cdot 4 - 5 \cdot 2) \, \mathbf{j} + ((-2) \cdot 2 - 5 \cdot (-2)) \, \mathbf{k} \\[5pt] & = -12 \, \mathbf{i} + 18 \, \mathbf{j} + 6 \,\mathbf{k} \\[5pt] & = \left\langle -12, 18, 6 \right\rangle \end{align*}

question.text: Find the limit $\displaystyle \lim_{t \to 1} \big[ \mathbf f(t) \cdot \mathbf g(t) \big]$ given that $\mathbf f(t)$ and $\mathbf g(t)$ are defined as: \begin{align*} \mathbf f(t) = \begin{bmatrix} \dfrac{\ln{t}}{t-1} \\ \dfrac{2\cos{\pi t}}{t} \\ \dfrac{2\sin{\pi t}}{t} \end{bmatrix}, \qquad \mathbf g(t) = \begin{bmatrix} \dfrac{t^2-2t+1}{t+1} \\ \dfrac{\ln{t}+t}{t+1} \\ \dfrac{e^{t+1}}{t+1} \end{bmatrix} \end{align*}
question.explanation:
First, we find the limit of each function:

\begin{align*} \lim_{t \to 1} \mathbf f(t) & = \begin{bmatrix} \displaystyle \lim_{t \to 1}\,\left(\dfrac{\ln{t}}{t-1}\right) \\[3pt] \displaystyle\lim_{t \to 1} \, \left(\dfrac{2\cos{\pi t}}{t}\right) \\[3pt] \displaystyle\lim_{t \to 1}\,\left(\dfrac{2\sin{\pi t}}{t} \right) \end{bmatrix} =\begin{bmatrix} \displaystyle \lim_{t \to 1}\,\left(\dfrac{(\ln{t})'}{(t-1)'}\right) \\[3pt] \displaystyle\lim_{t \to 1} \, \left(\dfrac{2\cos{\pi t}}{t}\right) \\[3pt] \displaystyle\lim_{t \to 1}\,\left(\dfrac{2\sin{\pi t}}{t} \right) \end{bmatrix} =\begin{bmatrix} \displaystyle \lim_{t \to 1}\,\left(\dfrac{1}{t}\right)\\[3pt] \displaystyle\dfrac{2\cos{\pi }}{1} \\[3pt] \displaystyle \dfrac{2\sin{\pi}}{1} \end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix} 1 \\ -2 \\ 0 \end{bmatrix} \end{align*}

Note that for the first component of $\displaystyle \lim_{t \to 1} \mathbf f(t)$ we used L'Hopital's Rule.

\begin{align*} \lim_{t \to 1} \mathbf g(t) & = \begin{bmatrix} \displaystyle\lim_{t \to 1}\,\dfrac{t^2-2t+1}{t+1} \\[3pt] \displaystyle\lim_{t \to 1} \,\dfrac{\ln{t}+t}{t+1} \\[3pt] \displaystyle\lim_{t \to 1}\,\dfrac{e^{t+1}}{t+1} \end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix} \displaystyle \dfrac{1^2-2\cdot 1+1}{1+1} \\[3pt] \displaystyle \dfrac{\ln{1}+1}{1+1} \\[3pt] \displaystyle \dfrac{e^{1+1}}{1+1} \end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix} 0 \\ \dfrac{1}{2} \\ \dfrac{e^2}{2} \end{bmatrix} \end{align*}

Now, we use properties of limits to calculate the final result:

\begin{align*} \lim_{t \to 1} \big[ \mathbf f(t) \cdot \mathbf g(t) \big] & = \lim_{t \to 1} \mathbf f(t) \cdot \lim_{t \to 1} \mathbf g(t) \\[3pt] & = \begin{bmatrix} 1 \\ -2 \\ 0 \end{bmatrix} \cdot \begin{bmatrix} 0 \\ \dfrac{1}{2} \\ \dfrac{e^2}{2} \end{bmatrix} \\[3pt] & =1 \cdot 0 + (-2) \cdot \dfrac{1}{2}+ 0 \cdot \dfrac{e^2}{2}\\[3pt] & =-1. \end{align*}

question.text: Find the limit $\displaystyle \lim_{t \to 0} \big[ \mathbf f(t) \cdot \mathbf g(t) \big]$ given that $\mathbf f(t)$ and $\mathbf g(t)$ are defined as: \begin{align*} \mathbf f(t) &= \left\langle \dfrac{t^2-2t+2}{t+1}, \: \dfrac{\sin{(2t)}}{t}, \: t\sin{t} \right\rangle \\[3pt] \mathbf g(t) &= \left\langle \dfrac {e^{2t}-1}{t}, \: 1-\cos{t}, \: t+1\right\rangle\end{align*}
question.explanation:
First, we find the limit of each function: \begin{align*} \lim_{t \to 0} \mathbf f(t) & = \left\langle \lim_{t \to 0} \dfrac{t^2-2t+2}{t+1} , \: \lim_{t \to 0}\dfrac{\sin{(2t)}}{t} , \: \lim_{t \to 0} t\sin{t} \right\rangle \\[7pt] & = \left\langle \lim_{t \to 0} \dfrac{t^2-2t+2}{t+1} , \: 2\lim_{t \to 0}\dfrac{\sin{(2t)}}{(2t)} , \: \lim_{t \to 0} t\sin{t} \right\rangle \\[7pt] & = \left\langle \dfrac{0^2-2\cdot 0+2}{0+1} , \: 2\cdot 1 , \: 0\cdot\sin{0} \right\rangle \\[7pt] & = \left\langle 2, 2, 0 \right\rangle \\[7pt] \end{align*}

Note that for the second component of $\displaystyle\lim_{t \to 0} \mathbf f(t)$ we used a special limit $\displaystyle\lim_{u\to 0}\dfrac{\sin{u}}{u}=1.$

\begin{align*} \lim_{t \to 0} \mathbf g(t) & = \left\langle \lim_{t \to 0}\dfrac {e^{2t}-1}{t} , \: \lim_{t \to 0} (1-\cos{t}) , \: \lim_{t \to 0} (t+1) \right\rangle \\[7pt] & = \left\langle \lim_{t \to 0}\dfrac {(e^{2t}-1)'}{(t)'} , \: \lim_{t \to 0} (1-\cos{t}) , \: \lim_{t \to 0} (t+1) \right\rangle \\[7pt] & = \left\langle \lim_{t \to 0}\dfrac {2e^{2t}}{1} , \: \lim_{t \to 0} (1-\cos{t}) , \: \lim_{t \to 0} (t+1) \right\rangle \\[7pt] & = \left\langle 2e^{0} , \: 1-\cos{0} , \: 0+1 \right\rangle \\[7pt] &= \left\langle 2, 0, 1 \right\rangle \end{align*} Note that for the first component of $\displaystyle\lim_{t \to 0} \mathbf g(t)$ we used L'Hopital's Rule.

Now, we use properties of limits to calculate the final result:

\begin{align*} \lim_{t \to 0} \big[ \mathbf f(t) \cdot \mathbf g(t) \big] & = \lim_{t \to 0} f(t) \cdot \lim_{t \to 0} \mathbf g(t) \\[3pt] & = \left\langle 2, \: 2, \: 0 \right\rangle \cdot \left\langle 2,0,1 \right\rangle \\[3pt] &= 2 \cdot 2 + 2\cdot 0 + 0 \cdot 1 \\[3pt] & = 4 \end{align*}

question.text: Find the limit $\displaystyle \lim_{t \to 0} \big[ \mathbf f(t) \cdot \mathbf g(t) \big]$ given that $\mathbf f(t)$ and $\mathbf g(t)$ are defined as \begin{align*} \mathbf f(t) = \begin{bmatrix} 3e^t \\ \tan{t} \\ \dfrac{t^2+9}{t+3} \end{bmatrix}, \qquad \mathbf g(t) = \begin{bmatrix} t-2 \\ \dfrac{3t-2}{t^2-1} \\ 2^t \end{bmatrix}. \end{align*}
question.explanation:
First, we find the limit of each function: \begin{align*} \lim_{t \to 0} \mathbf f(t) & = \begin{bmatrix} \displaystyle \lim_{t \to 0} 3e^t \\ \displaystyle \lim_{t \to 0} \tan{t} \\ \displaystyle \lim_{t \to 0} \dfrac{t^2+9}{t+3} \end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix} 3e^0 \\ \tan{0} \\ \dfrac{0^2+9}{0+3} \end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix} 3 \\ 0 \\ 3 \end{bmatrix}\\[10pt] \lim_{t \to 0} \mathbf g(t) & = \begin{bmatrix} \displaystyle \lim_{t \to 0} \, (t - 2) \\ \displaystyle \lim_{t \to 0} \dfrac{3t-2}{t^2-1} \\ \displaystyle \lim_{t \to 0} 2^t \end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix} 0-2 \\ \dfrac{3(0)-2}{0^2-1} \\ 2^0 \end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix} -2 \\ 2 \\ 1 \end{bmatrix} \end{align*}

Now, we use properties of limits to calculate the final result:

\begin{align*} \lim_{t \to 0} \big[ \mathbf f(t) \cdot \mathbf g(t) \big] & = \lim_{t \to 0} \mathbf f(t) \cdot \lim_{t \to 0} \mathbf g(t) \\[5pt] & = \begin{bmatrix} 3 \\ 0 \\ 3 \end{bmatrix} \cdot \begin{bmatrix} -2 \\ 2 \\ 1 \end{bmatrix} \\[5pt] & = 3(-2) + 0(2) + 3(1) \\[5pt] & =-3 \end{align*}

question.text: Find the limit $\displaystyle \lim_{t \to \pi} \big[ \mathbf f(t) \cdot \mathbf g(t) \big]$ given that $\mathbf f(t)$ and $\mathbf g(t)$ are defined as: \begin{align*} \mathbf f(t) = \begin{bmatrix} \sin t \\ 1+ \cos t \\ \dfrac {4 t} {\pi} \end{bmatrix}, \qquad \mathbf g(t) = \begin{bmatrix} \cos t \\ 2+ \tan t \\ \cos t \end{bmatrix} \end{align*}
question.explanation:
First, we find the limit of each function:

\begin{align*} \lim_{t \to \pi} \mathbf f(t) & = \begin{bmatrix} \displaystyle \lim_{t \to \pi}\,( \sin t) \\ \displaystyle\lim_{t \to \pi} \, (1+ \cos t) \\ \displaystyle\lim_{t \to \pi}\,\left(\dfrac {4 t} {\pi} \right) \end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix} \sin \pi \\ 1+ \cos \pi \\ \dfrac {4 \pi} {\pi} \end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix} 0 \\ 0 \\ 4 \end{bmatrix} \\[7pt] \lim_{t \to \pi} \mathbf g(t) & = \begin{bmatrix} \displaystyle\lim_{t \to \pi}\,(\cos t) \\ \displaystyle\lim_{t \to \pi} \,(2+ \tan t) \\ \displaystyle\lim_{t \to \pi}\,(\cos t) \end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix} \cos \pi \\ (2+ \tan \pi) \\ \cos \pi \end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix} -1 \\ 2 \\ -1 \end{bmatrix} \end{align*}

Now, we use properties of limits to calculate the final result:

\begin{align*} \lim_{t \to \pi} \big[ \mathbf f(t) \cdot \mathbf g(t) \big] & = \lim_{t \to \pi} \mathbf f(t) \cdot \lim_{t \to \pi} \mathbf g(t) \\[3pt] & = \begin{bmatrix} 0 \\ 0 \\ 4 \end{bmatrix} \cdot \begin{bmatrix} -1 \\ 2 \\ -1 \end{bmatrix} \\[3pt] & =0 \cdot (-1) + 0 \cdot 2 + 4 \cdot (-1)\\[3pt] & =-4. \end{align*}
